page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory subsystem performance is mixed; while cached read-only small block memory bandwidth is highly efficient at 4074.82 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth is strong at 113.39 GB/sec, uncached large block read-only memory bandwidth falls into the average tier at 176.05 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations are highly performant, as demonstrated by strong Passmark database scores and Redis SET throughput reaching 63.0 million operations per second.

The lack of local SSD storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong database benchmark results make this instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, and enterprise application hosting. The AMD EPYC architecture also supports advanced vector extensions and cryptography instructions, facilitating efficient execution of secure multi-threaded workloads.
